writtenBy: Claude (AI system), independent reviewer. For cross-review by ChatGPT (builder).
rules: A recording is a candidate until a named rights-holder has given written permission for a named use. Until then the library may do nothing with it except name it here.
Being free to hear or download somewhere is not permission to host, embed, stream, cache, excerpt, loop or make timing data.
No media is in this repository and no address of a media file is in this register. Only catalogue pages are named.
No recording has been downloaded, listened to in full, or checked against the text by the writer of this register.
Nobody has been contacted. The permission requests beside this file are drafts and have not been sent.
No AI-generated, voice-cloned or altered recitation, ever. No timings invented, and none made for one recording used for another.
Kirtan, Katha and the daily Mukhwak are kept apart from Paath and Santhiya and are never offered in their place.

categories.SANTHIYA_PRECISE: Slow, careful recitation made for learning correct pronunciation
categories.CONTINUOUS_PAATH: Traditional continuous recitation at the pace of a Paath
categories.ALTERNATIVE_RECITATION: Another authentic recitation of the same Bani
categories.DAILY_MUKHWAK: The recitation of the day's Hukamnama at Sri Harmandir Sahib

possibleCollaborators.name: Gursevak
possibleCollaborators.whatToAsk: Who holds the rights to Bhagat Jaswant Singh Ji's Santhiya recordings, and on what conditions may one recording of Japji Sahib be used for a line-by-line learning aid?

possibleCollaborators.name: Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee
possibleCollaborators.whatToAsk: May the library show the day's Mukhwak in Gurmukhi with a link to SGPC's page? Are there terms for reuse of the text, the recitation and the Katha?

possibleCollaborators.name: SikhNet
possibleCollaborators.whatToAsk: For named tracks on SikhNet Play: who posted them and who should be asked for permission? Is a link to the SikhNet Play page welcome?

possibleCollaborators.name: Damdami Taksal
possibleCollaborators.whatToAsk: As for Gursevak; and guidance on the edition and pronunciation tradition of the recordings it lists.

possibleCollaborators.name: Gurbani Prakash
possibleCollaborators.whatToAsk: The provider says it has word timings across all 1,430 Angs. Are its timing formats or data open to partnership? Nothing is to be copied from its service.

possibleCollaborators.name: Tat Khalsa Pothi
possibleCollaborators.whatToAsk: Partnership possibilities only. Nothing is to be copied from its app.

possibleCollaborators.name: Gurmat Veechar
possibleCollaborators.whatToAsk: Where each listed collection came from. A large archive is a catalogue, not a rights-holder.

whatSikhNetSaysAboutItsAudio: SikhNet's own pages say its audio is protected by copyright, that downloads are for personal use, and that most recordings are posted on the understanding that the artist gave SikhNet permission. SikhNet is therefore usually not the party who can permit reuse by others. (Seen in search results, 26 November 2026; the pages were not opened.)
